questions.questionText: In farming, what is an example of what economists call capital?

options.text: savings the farmer has in the bank
shares in a farming company
the money the farmer set aside to pay taxes
the tractor owned by the farmer

questions.questionText: What would cause an outward shift of a country’s production possibility curve (PPC)?

options.text: a fall in unemployment
an increase in the rate of income tax
an increase in the labour force
a reduction in expenditure on education

questions.questionText:
In recent years more golf courses, which use large quantities of water, have opened in China.
What may be the opportunity cost of this?

options.text: cost of water
loss of farmland
sales of golf equipment
wages of golf course staff

questions.questionText: What is a characteristic of tertiary industries?

options.text: They are located away from centres of population.
They do not sell to the final consumer.
They tend to be labour-intensive.
They transform raw materials into goods.

questions.questionText:
China has built a new railway in Kenya from the capital, Nairobi, to the seaport of Mombasa.
Kenya must repay the cost of the railway to China. Journey time has been reduced significantly
but fares have increased and farmers have lost agricultural land along the new line.
Who bears the external costs of this operation?

options.text: China who built the new railway
farmers who have lost agricultural land
Kenya who must repay the cost to China
passengers who pay the higher fare

questions.questionText: What is meant by equilibrium in a market?

options.text: where products offered for sale equal consumer demand
where profit is at the expected level
where the quantity of inputs equals the quantity of output
where total costs equal total revenue

questions.questionText:
A product has a price elasticity of demand of –0.5.
What happens to the demand for a product if its price falls from $1 to $0.80?

options.text: It decreases by 10%.
It decreases by 20%.
It increases by 10%.
It increases by 20%.

questions.questionText:
The demand for gas in a country becomes price-inelastic.
What will happen as a result?

options.text: Gas workers will be less likely to be successful in obtaining wage increases.
Gas workers will be more likely to be successful in obtaining wage increases.
Total expenditure on gas by consumers will fall when its price rises.
Total expenditure on gas by consumers will rise when its price falls.

questions.questionText: Which advantage do coins have that make them more suitable than banknotes to act as money?

options.text: They are more divisible.
They are more durable.
They are more portable.
They are more recognisable.

questions.questionText: What is the most important factor that affects how much a family saves?

options.text: the income of the family
the level of taxation
the rate of inflation
the reliability of banks

questions.questionText:
The table shows the change in real incomes for a number of occupations between 1985 and
2015.
change in
occupation real income
doctors 153
lawyers 114
accountants 60
bricklayers 37
bus and coach drivers 19
fork-lift truck drivers –5
What can be concluded from the table?

options.text: All occupations were better off in 2015 than in 1985.
Fork-lift truck drivers earned the lowest wages in 2015.
Doctors have earned more than lawyers since 1985.
Professionals received higher percentage increases in income than manual workers.

questions.questionText: Which business organisation is most likely to have unlimited liability?

options.text: co-operative
multinational
public limited company
sole trader

questions.questionText: What is an example of a technical economy of scale?

options.text: Banks provide loans at a lower interest rate to bigger firms.
Bigger firms hire more workers.
Firms obtain discounts when buying in bulk.
Machines are used closer to their full capacity.

questions.questionText:
Which form of taxation always takes an increasing percentage of the taxpayer’s income as it
rises?

options.text: indirect
progressive
proportionate
regressive

questions.questionText: What is the most likely effect of a government reducing the money supply?

options.text: Employment will decrease.
Growth will increase.
Inflation will increase.
Tax rates will decrease.

questions.questionText:
Sometimes the government regulates the market to protect the interests of consumers.
Which kind of regulation would achieve this protection?

options.text: discouraging economies of scale that lead to lower costs
preventing mergers which result in high monopoly prices
reducing shop opening hours
reducing the range of products supplied to the market

questions.questionText: Why might GDP per head be underestimated in a developed economy?

options.text: It does not account for changes in population.
It does not include financial services output.
It does not include the hidden economy.
It does not take into account the primary sector.

questions.questionText: What is included in the Human Development Index (HDI)?

options.text: gender inequality
life expectancy at birth
political freedom
the impact of pollution

questions.questionText:
What is most likely to have caused a long-term decrease in the numbers employed in the banking
sector of an economy?

options.text: frictional unemployment caused by relocating a bank’s headquarters
seasonal unemployment caused by reduced customer demand in the summer
technological unemployment caused by an increase in internet banking
voluntary unemployment caused by a reduction in wage rates

questions.questionText: What might cause prices to rise because of cost-push inflation?

options.text: an increase in government spending on education
an increase in household consumption
an increase in the balance of payments surplus
an increase in wages and salaries

questions.questionText: Which action might be taken by an economy wishing to produce a greater range of products?

options.text: concentrate on the production of primary products
encourage imports of manufactured goods
encourage investment by multinational companies
increase interest rates

questions.questionText:
Given the following information, which country is most likely to have the highest standard of
living?
birth death life infant
rate rate expectancy mortality rate

options.text: Bangladesh 27 10 58 93
Bhutan 36 14 53 107
Botswana 31 21 40 57
Brunei 25 5 72 22

questions.questionText:
In a country the birth rate increased but the population decreased.
What could have happened to other factors to cause this?

options.text: a fall in infant mortality but no change in the death rate
a rise in net immigration but no change in the death rate
no change in migration but the death rate rose
the death rate fell with no change in migration

questions.questionText:
The US government decides to reduce the size of the quota on a good it buys from China.
What is likely to happen?

options.text: The good will become cheaper in the US.
The US balance of trade will worsen.
The US government’s revenue will decline.
There will be less of the good imported into the US.

questions.questionText:
Changes in the foreign exchange rate of a country resulted in a depreciation of its currency.
What is not likely to happen?

options.text: The costs of imported raw materials will fall.
The country’s export trading position will become more competitive.
The country’s residents will find it more expensive to take holidays abroad.
The current account deficit will be unchanged.

questions.questionText:
Which item will register as an outflow on the services section of the current account of the US
balance of payments?

options.text: money paid by chemical producers in the US for foreign oil
money paid by foreign firms for US cars
money paid by migrant workers in the US to their families overseas
money paid by US tourists visiting attractions in other countries

questions.questionText:
A large amount of the agricultural products in a country were damaged by floods.
What is likely to have happened to the price of agricultural products and the volume of imports of
agricultural products?
price of products volume of imports

options.text: fall fall
fall rise
rise fall
